subtitle: On the Unconquerable Mountain: Ajayaraja, Somalekha and the Birth of Ajayameru

panels.shot: epic wide of a rugged Aravalli hill with a nascent fort-town rising, low sun casting long shadows, Ajayaraja II in the foreground looking over plans and silver coins
panels.action: Ajayaraja II stands on a wind-swept Aravalli ridge above the bare hill that will become Ajayameru, one hand resting on his sword, the other open over a small tray of freshly struck silver coins.

dialogue.text: In the twelfth century, Ajayaraja of the Chahamanas left the salt lakes of Sambhar, climbed a bare Aravalli hill, named it Ajayameru — and sent his queen’s name glittering along the desert roads in silver.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी में चाहमन अजयराज सांभर की खारी झीलें छोड़कर नंगे अरावली टीले पर चढ़ा, उसे अजयमेरु नाम दिया — और रानी का नाम रजत में रेगिस्तानी राहों पर दौड़ा दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high above Sambhar Lake to the bustling old capital on its shore
panels.action: From the shimmering expanse of Sambhar Lake, the view closes in on the dense streets and low fortifications of the old Chahamana capital, with Ajayaraja II in council on a terrace overlooking the waters.

dialogue.text: Before the hill of Ajayameru, there was Sambhar — the salt lake, the old Chahamana seat, the familiar walls that had long guarded their line.

i18n.hi: अजयमेरु की पहाड़ी से पहले था सांभर — नमक झील, पुराना चाहमन राजधानी, वही दीवारें जो पीढ़ियों से उनकी वंश-रक्षा कर रही थीं।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot in a dim council chamber with maps and metalwork on a low table
panels.action: Ajayaraja II leans over a rough map showing Sambhar and the Aravalli hills, small clay forts placed upon it, while in the foreground a craftsman shows a blank silver flan on his palm.

dialogue.text: To the west, the Aravalli ridges; to the east, the routes from Malwa and Delhi; to the north-west, the memory of Ghaznavid raids. Sambhar was rich — but was it safe?

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में अरावली की शृंखलाएँ; पूर्व में मालवा और दिल्ली की राहें; उत्तर-पश्चिम में ग़ज़नवी हमलों की छाया। सांभर समृद्ध था — पर क्या सुरक्षित था?

panels.shot: wide tracking shot of a Ghaznavid force riding across desert scrub toward Chahamana territory
panels.action: A distant line of mailed horsemen bearing eastern banners rides in loose formation across scrubby desert, dust rising around them, while a Chahamana outpost watchtower stands tense on a nearby rise.

dialogue.text: Some years before, a Ghaznavid force had tested these lands. Chahamana arms held them, but the shock remained: the frontier was porous, the plains exposed.

i18n.hi: कुछ वर्ष पहले ग़ज़नवी सेना ने इन धरतीों को परखा था। चाहमन तलवारें टिक गईं, पर सदमा रह गया: सरहद छिद्रदार, मैदान खुले।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a rocky Aravalli hilltop, Ajayaraja on horseback surveying the landscape
panels.action: Ajayaraja II, in mail and turban, sits astride a horse on a craggy Aravalli outcrop, his gaze sweeping over a bare hill opposite, its rocky shoulders rising above scattered thorn trees and distant caravan paths.

dialogue.text: So the king rode the hills. On a stony ridge he saw it — a high back of rock, overlooking routes and lakes, a place where wind, not enemy cavalry, ruled.

i18n.hi: तभी राजा ने पहाड़ियाँ टटोलीं। पत्थरीली कटक पर उसे दिखी — ऊँची चट्टान की पीठ, राहों और झीलों पर झुकी, जहाँ हवा राज करती थी, दुश्मन घुड़सवार नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot profile of Ajayaraja, with wind tugging at his cloak as he points to the hill
panels.action: Wind tugs Ajayaraja II’s cloak as he stands, arm outstretched, pointing toward the bare hill, his face lit by a fierce, decisive resolve.

dialogue.text: Later poets would call it Ajayameru — the unconquerable mountain. Whether village or shrine stood there before, the record is quiet. But under Ajayaraja, the hill became a capital.

i18n.hi: बाद के कवि इसे अजयमेरु — अजेय पर्वत — कहेंगे। पहले वहाँ बस गाँव था या देवस्थान, लेख चुप हैं। पर अजयराज के अधीन वही टीला राजधानी बना।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of early fortification works on the hill, lines of workers and stone being hauled up
panels.action: From above, lines of workers haul stone blocks up rough paths, new walls snaking along the hill’s crest, while Ajayaraja II watches from a temporary pavilion of canvas and wood.

dialogue.text: Stones moved, walls grew. The Prithviraja-Vijaya would sing of Ajayameru’s glory, but its beginning was sweat, rope, and the scrape of stone on stone.

i18n.hi: पत्थर हिले, दीवारें उगीं। पृथ्वीराज-विजय अजयमेरु की महिमा गाएगा, पर शुरुआत केवल पसीना, रस्सी, और पत्थर पर पत्थर की खराश थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Paramara army banner in the distance and Chahamana troops forming ranks on a plain below the hills
panels.action: On a plain below the Aravalli foothills, Ajayaraja II’s armored infantry and cavalry form ordered ranks, while in the hazy distance standards of the Paramara king Naravarman flutter above his host.

dialogue.text: To the south, the Paramara king Naravarman watched this rising power. War came, and the Chahamana king met him — the chronicles remember Ajayaraja’s victory.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में परमार नरेश नरवर्मन इस उभरती शक्ति को ताक रहे थे। युद्ध हुआ, और चाहमन राजा उनसे भिड़ा — आख्यान अजयराज की विजय याद रखते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of Ajayaraja on horseback after battle, troops behind him, the hill of Ajayameru faintly visible
panels.action: Dust still hangs in the air as Ajayaraja II sits firm on his horse, his troops behind him raising spears in quiet salute, while far beyond them the outline of the Ajayameru hill stands against the sky.

dialogue.text: The victory did more than humble a rival. It told the desert and the hills that Ajayaraja’s new seat was not a retreat, but a rock from which he could strike.

i18n.hi: यह विजय सिर्फ़ प्रतिद्वंदी को झुकाना नहीं थी। उसने रेगिस्तान और पहाड़ियों को बता दिया कि अजयराज की नई गद्दी पलायन नहीं, वह शिला है जहाँ से वार होगा।

panels.shot: intimate indoor shot of a royal mint, with dies and hammers on a bench, Ajayaraja supervising
panels.action: Inside a stone-walled mint, artisans sit at low benches with dies and hammers, a small furnace glowing, while Ajayaraja II stands over them, examining a newly struck silver coin in his hand.

dialogue.text: Yet stone walls alone do not make a capital. Silver sang of Ajayameru. The king ordered new drammas — round, bright, the weight of the realm in a palm.

i18n.hi: पर अकेली पत्थर की दीवारें राजधानी नहीं बनातीं। चाँदी ने अजयमेरु का गान गाया। राजा ने नए द्रम्म जारी किए — गोल, उजले, एक हथेली में राज का वज़न।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a freshly struck silver coin still on the anvil, the die lifted away
panels.action: A hammer has just lifted from a glowing-silver coin on an anvil, its design crisp, minute letters along the edge catching the light, with Ajayaraja II’s fingers moving in to take it.

dialogue.text: On those coins, numismatists today trace a striking choice: along with Ajayaraja’s authority, the name of his queen, Somalekha, appears — her presence struck in silver.

i18n.hi: इन सिक्कों पर आधुनिक नुमिस्माताओं ने एक साहसी चयन पकड़ा: अजयराज की सत्ता के साथ उनकी रानी सोअलेखा का नाम भी है — उसका अस्तित्व चाँदी में उकेरा गया।

panels.shot: soft-lit mid-shot in the palace, Ajayaraja offering a small tray of new coins toward an unseen queen
panels.action: In a gently lit palace chamber, Ajayaraja II holds out a tray of freshly minted coins toward the veiled figure of Queen Somalekha just at the frame’s edge, his expression half-proud, half-playful.

dialogue.text: Jayanaka, in the Prithviraja-Vijaya, would boast that Somalekha was ‘used to freshly minted coins every day’ — praise and exaggeration, but built on a truth stamped into metal.

i18n.hi: पृथ्वीराज-विजय के जयनक ने शेख़ी बघारी कि सोअलेखा ‘हर रोज़ नए सिक्कों की आदी थी’ — प्रशंसा और अतिशयोक्ति, पर उस धातु में गड़ी सच्चाई पर टिकी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling Ajayameru market street under the hillfort, merchants trading with coins in hand
panels.action: Below the rising hillfort, a busy market street teems with traders exchanging small pouches, silver coins glittering as they change hands, the hill of Ajayameru looming above them.

dialogue.text: Those drammas did not sit in coffers. They moved — along camel caravans, to cloth-sellers and horse-dealers, through the hands of men who spoke of the hill-city from which they came.

i18n.hi: वे द्रम्म खज़ानों में नहीं जमे रहे। वे चले — ऊँट-कारवाँ के संग, कपड़ा-बिक्री और घोड़ा-बाज़ारों तक, उन हाथों से होकर जो उस पहाड़ी-नगरी की बातें करते थे जहाँ से वे आए थे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of desert caravan at dusk, traders examining a coin by firelight with the queen’s name faintly visible
panels.action: By a small desert campfire, two traders sit cross-legged, one holding a silver coin up to the flickering light, its tiny inscription with Somalekha’s name just visible as he studies it with curiosity.

dialogue.text: “Ajayameru’s queen,” says one trader softly. “Her name rides with their silver.”

i18n.hi: “अजयमेरु की रानी,” एक सौदागर धीमे कहता है। “उनकी चाँदी पर उसका नाम सफ़र करता है।”

panels.shot: heroic wide inside the completed hillfort, Ajayaraja at a balcony overlooking city and distant Sambhar Lake
panels.action: Within the finished ramparts of Ajayameru, Ajayaraja II stands at a high balcony, looking out over tiled roofs clustered on the slopes and, far on the horizon, the pale shimmer of Sambhar Lake.

dialogue.text: Was Ajayameru a fresh carving on bare rock, or the raising of an older shrine-town into a capital? Scholars differ, and the stones keep their counsel.

i18n.hi: अजयमेरु नंगे पत्थर पर नया नक़्श था, या पुराने देव-नगर को राजधानी की ऊँचाई पर उठाना? विद्वान बँटे हैं, और पत्थर ख़ुद चुप हैं।

panels.shot: stylised split-view: on one side a copy of Prithviraja-Vijaya’s poetic imagining of Ajayameru, on the other a modern scholar in a study with coins and maps
panels.action: On the left, a stylised court poet recites before a king, an illuminated manuscript of the Prithviraja-Vijaya before him; on the right, a modern scholar at a desk studies Ajayaraja coins and a map of Ajmer.

dialogue.text: Jayanaka would claim that even Lanka and Dvaraka were unfit for Ajayameru’s maidservants — panegyric, not gazetteer. Between his praise-poem, stones, and coins, historians piece the city’s true rise.

i18n.hi: जयनक दावा करेगा कि लंका और द्वारका भी अजयमेरु की दासियों के लायक नहीं — यह प्रशस्ति है, भूगोल नहीं। उसकी स्तुति, पत्थर और सिक्कों के बीच से इतिहासकार नगरी के असली उभार को जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: serene dusk-wide of Ajayameru hill silhouetted, lights of the town glowing below, a coin large in the foreground
panels.action: At dusk, the silhouette of Ajayameru’s hillfort crowns the horizon, small lamps of the town glowing below, while in the foreground a single Ajayaraja silver coin lies half-buried in sand, its edges catching the last light.

dialogue.text: A city on a hill, a queen’s name on a coin: Ajayaraja’s choices turned terrain into message and metal into memory, so that long after his reign, Ajmer’s stones and silver still speak his age.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी पर नगर, सिक्के पर रानी का नाम: अजयराज के चुनावों ने भूभाग को संदेश, और धातु को स्मृति बना दिया, ताकि उनके बाद भी अजयमेरु की शिलाएँ और चाँदी उनकी युग-कथा कहती रहें।

title_i18n.en: Ajayaraja Founds the Hill of Ajmer
title_i18n.hi: अजयराज ने बसाया अजयमेरु की पहाड़ी

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Unconquerable Mountain: Ajayaraja, Somalekha and the Birth of Ajayameru
subtitle_i18n.hi: अजेय पर्वत पर: अजयराज, सोअलेखा और अजयमेरु का जन्म
